audit.recode_to: fixed-dominant (penultimate; regular antepenult subclass = bases ending in geminate + historically added /a/, i.e. the paragogic syllable is not counted), domain word/base; cite Utsumi 2013 §2.3.4 p. 322 as co-deciding source with Sneddon 1984 p. 22, and fix the comparative locator to §2.3.23 p. 53. Alternative if the catalog treats the Sangiric paragoge as extrametrical (as for Sangir): keep fixed penult but drop counts as exceptionless (the strict set) and state the domain explicitly.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: confirmed verbatim at §2.1.3.2 printed p. 22 in our held Sneddon 1984 text (held under bant1286/rata1244, not under tala1285); comparative section is §2.3.23 p. 53, not 2.3.24. (2) Source: a 1984 comparative monograph whose Talaud phonology rests on a self-declared 'very brief study'; every source that speaks to Talaud stress hedges: Talens/Adriani 1911 'de meeste woorden' penult with the loose -a syllable not counted; Sneddon 1984 'usually' penult, 'often' antepenult before the added a, 'cases which do not conform'; Utsumi 2013 (held, first-hand fieldwork, the best available statement) default penult, antepenult in 'the majority' of geminate+/a/ trisyllabic bases, 'largely predictable'. (3) Our record codes fixed-strict penult (counts as exceptionless (the strict set), rule 10/010/0010..) with domain not stated by the source, which no source supports on the surface: a large lexical class (u'ritta, e'sakka) is antepenul

sources.quote: 'Daar de meeste woorden den klemtoon op de voorlaatste lettergreep hebben, komt de looze lettergreep dus twee plaatsen na den klemtoon te staan' (p. 6); §5: the loose final syllable (original final consonant + short a) 'telt niet voor vol; de klemtoon blijft onveranderd op de syllabe die hem had' (p. 6-7). I.e. penultimate stress in most words; the paragogic -a syllable is not counted, giving surface antepenult.
sources.locator: printed pp. 6-7 (§4-5 'De looze eindlettergreep'; pdf pp. 11-12); also p. ~20 (djvu line 1024): stress rules of Adriani's Sangireesche Spraakkunst pp. 14-20 'in hoofdzaak ook voor het Talaoetsch gelden'
sources.note: Earliest description; states penult stress for 'most words' with the paragogic -a syllable not counted (pp. 6-7), the same analysis Sneddon and Utsumi give; now obtained.
